personality: Calm and commanding, not a damsel. She walked to the lake herself.

cards.title: The King's Daughter
cards.text: She was the only daughter of the king of Silene. When the lot fell on her, her father offered the people his gold, his silver and half his kingdom to spare her. They refused him: their own children had gone to the lake, and so must his. He was given eight days. When they were over, he dressed her as a bride, kissed her, and let her go.

source.author: Jacobus de Voragine, c. 1260; English by William Caxton, 1483
source.edition: Temple Classics, ed. F. S. Ellis, 1900

cards.title: At the Water's Edge
cards.text: She waited alone by the lake. A young knight rode up and asked why she wept, and her first words to him were a warning: ride on, before you die with me. He stayed. When the dragon fell wounded he told her to tie her girdle round its neck, and she did. It was she, not the knight, who led the beast through the gates of Silene.

source.author: Jacobus de Voragine, c. 1260; English by William Caxton, 1483
source.edition: Temple Classics, ed. F. S. Ellis, 1900

cards.title: The Spring at the Altar
cards.text: After the dragon was slain, the king and twenty thousand of his people were baptised. Where her life had been bargained away, the king built a great church to Our Lady and St George. The legend says a spring rose from its altar, and its water healed every sick person who drank it.

source.author: Jacobus de Voragine, c. 1260; English by William Caxton, 1483
source.edition: Temple Classics, ed. F. S. Ellis, 1900
